visual.name: finstack-theme
visual.docs: Shared light/dark theme. Import styles/finstack/theme.css after Tailwind. Set data-theme and data-density on the app root. Colours, fonts, the type scale and the chart palettes are CSS variables from one token file: rebrand by generating this stylesheet from a brand file with a checkout of the registry (node finstack-quant-ui/scripts/gen-theme.mjs --brand <brand.json> --out <theme.css>) or by redeclaring variables on [data-theme] after it. IBM Plex Sans and Mono are supplied by pinned Fontsource packages under SIL OFL-1.1; no font binaries are copied into registry files.

visual.name: field-frame
visual.docs: Controlled field-frame primitive. Import the installed finstack theme. Supply canonical values, labels, constraints and option lists; this item owns presentation only. No worker or workbench is required.

visual.name: finstack-table
visual.docs: Controlled finstack-table primitive. Import the installed finstack theme. Supply canonical values, labels, constraints and option lists; this item owns presentation only. A column whose meta sets rowHeader renders its body cells as row headers (th scope=row) with plain-cell styling and selection. No worker or workbench is required.

visual.name: table-envelope
visual.docs: Display-only table-envelope primitive. Import the installed finstack theme. Pass the TableEnvelope a Rust table function returned (for example statements_analytics.plSummaryReport or Performance#summary) and a caption. Columns and rows keep their native order; numeric columns are right-aligned with every supplied digit; nothing is sorted, grouped, totalled, rounded or converted. No worker or workbench is required.

visual.name: enum-field
visual.docs: Controlled enum-field primitive. Import the installed finstack theme. Supply canonical values, labels, constraints and option lists; this item owns presentation only. No worker or workbench is required.

visual.name: json-viewer
visual.docs: Read-only JSON with lossless formatted presentation and an Original toggle. Numeric tokens remain exact. Invalid JSON, including duplicate keys, stays in Original view with a formatting notice. Copy and download always preserve the supplied bytes. Import the installed finstack theme; no worker or workbench is required.

visual.name: id-combobox
visual.docs: Controlled id-combobox primitive. Import the installed finstack theme. Supply canonical values, labels, constraints and option lists; this item owns presentation only. No worker or workbench is required. Composes the stock shadcn Combobox with controlled free text, supplied filtered suggestions and TanStack list virtualization; IDs are never inferred.

visual.name: finstack-chart
visual.docs: Standalone native SVG publication figure with complete titles, captions, sources and exports. Supply native chart definitions for scale/axis/unit conventions and annotation marks. Import the theme; no WASM, forms, tables or worker runtime is required. Export needs a same-origin font stylesheet and explicit dimensions.

visual.name: figure-example
visual.docs: Standalone supplied-data publication example. Uses the same figure props on screen and in explicit 900x600 vector / 1800x1200 pixel exports (6x4 inches at 300 PPI). The theme includes licensed fonts; install IBM Plex Sans in a desktop editor if it cannot use embedded webfonts.

visual.name: finstack-form
visual.docs: Shared TanStack Form contexts bound to registry fields, array controls, error summary and submit/reset controls. Values remain working edits; canonical validation is a separate boundary.

visual.name: decimal-input
visual.docs: Controlled decimal-input primitive. Import the installed finstack theme. Supply canonical values, labels, constraints and option lists; this item owns presentation only. No worker or workbench is required.

visual.name: money-input
visual.docs: Controlled money-input primitive. Import the installed finstack theme. Supply canonical values, labels, constraints and option lists; this item owns presentation only. No worker or workbench is required.

visual.name: rate-input
visual.docs: Controlled rate-input primitive. Import the installed finstack theme. Supply canonical values, labels, constraints and option lists; this item owns presentation only. No worker or workbench is required.

visual.name: tenor-input
visual.docs: Controlled tenor-input primitive. Import the installed finstack theme. Supply canonical values, labels, constraints and option lists; this item owns presentation only. No worker or workbench is required.

visual.name: day-count-select
visual.docs: Controlled day-count-select primitive. Import the installed finstack theme. Supply canonical values, labels, constraints and option lists; this item owns presentation only. No worker or workbench is required.

visual.name: bdc-select
visual.docs: Controlled bdc-select primitive. Import the installed finstack theme. Supply canonical values, labels, constraints and option lists; this item owns presentation only. No worker or workbench is required.

visual.name: knot-table
visual.docs: Controlled knot-table primitive. Import the installed finstack theme. Supply canonical values, labels, constraints and option lists; this item owns presentation only. No worker or workbench is required.

visual.name: money-value
visual.docs: Controlled money-value primitive. Import the installed finstack theme. Supply canonical values, labels, constraints and option lists; this item owns presentation only. No worker or workbench is required.

visual.name: date-input
visual.docs: Controlled date-input primitive. Import the installed finstack theme. Supply canonical values, labels, constraints and option lists; this item owns presentation only. No worker or workbench is required.

visual.name: domain-field
visual.docs: Date and decimal fields bound to the shared form context. Supply labels and constraints; canonical validation stays outside these controls.

visual.name: curve-chart
visual.docs: Displays validated CurveState entries with point-only stored coordinates. Variants are faceted, same-variant curves overlay. Base-correlation arrays and parametric fields retain their generated schema view. Native figure axes, annotations, typed callbacks, tooltip and per-variant exports are supported; linking requires a caller key mapping. No sampling or pricing engine.

visual.name: market-context-form
visual.docs: Complete market editor using generated schema/meta and native validation. Edit curves, FX entries, prices, stored surfaces, SABR cubes and FX ATM/RR/BF quotes; other data stays read-only and is retained. Import canonical JSON or a calibration envelope final_market. Supply useMarketValidator and receive complete canonical JSON on submit.

visual.name: vol-surface-chart
visual.docs: Canonical stored volatility heatmap, node table and exact row/column slices. Supply validated surface metadata and an explicit raw-unit color extent. Optional shared selection links caller controls; no interpolation or worker dependency. Import the shared theme. FX quote arrays remain separate from stored grids.

visual.name: fx-delta-quotes
visual.docs: Raw canonical FX ATM delta-neutral straddle, RR and BF quote arrays. Missing optional arrays remain missing. No forward, interpolation, strike grid or conversion is inferred.

visual.name: fx-matrix-grid
visual.docs: Exact directed stored FX matrices separated by pair-global, provider and date/policy-pinned sources. Missing cells remain unavailable, undated tuples stay undated, and complete config/state exports remain unchanged. No priority resolution, inverse rates or triangulation.

visual.name: market-context-browser
visual.docs: Searchable disclosure tree over every actual market value and generated root fields. Inspect exact leaf JSON and matching stored curve/FX views. Optional surfaceOptions supplies explicit color extents; without them surface data remains raw. A host renderObject slot can supply evaluated views with explicit strike/forward/convention inputs. No worker is required for stored browsing. Parent accepts canonical market edits through market-context-form/use-market-validator.

visual.name: schema-form
visual.docs: Generated schema form for any generated contract module. Supply a lazy generated module and native validation callback; canonical JSON is emitted after valid submission. Maps use editable key/value rows internally and emit exact string keys. Basic layout collapses defaulted or empty values under Less common terms. Composing editors inject disclosure, sheet and promotedField to group domain terms, choose the term-sheet root and promote one input.

visual.name: curve-link-example
visual.docs: Stored discount curve table and chart share accepted semantic selection. Explicit row/cell addresses preserve original data and render identity; caller activation callbacks update detail only. No WASM or financial calculations.

visual.name: metric-picker
visual.docs: Controlled metric-picker primitive. Import the installed finstack theme. Supply canonical values, labels, constraints and option lists; this item owns presentation only. No worker or workbench is required.

visual.name: measure-value
visual.docs: Controlled measure-value primitive. Import the installed finstack theme. Supply canonical values, labels, constraints and option lists; this item owns presentation only. No worker or workbench is required.

visual.name: stamp-badge
visual.docs: Controlled stamp-badge primitive. Import the installed finstack theme. Supply canonical values, labels, constraints and option lists; this item owns presentation only. No worker or workbench is required.

visual.name: valuation-summary
visual.docs: Displays supplied valuation context and raw measures. Comparisons retain independent currencies and stamps; no local differences, aggregates or FX conversion. Pass native metric groups and explicit source-backed units when available.

visual.name: measures-grid
visual.docs: Displays supplied valuation context and measures. Labels are the native metric id in sentence case with recognised acronyms upper-cased; native metric metadata groups bucket tenors in maturity order; Exact keys reveals fully qualified keys. Values default to six significant digits, with Exact values and value titles retaining supplied precision. The nonzero view hides zero rows only when both sides are supplied and zero in a comparison; Show all reveals every row, and missing values remain distinct. Comparisons retain independent currencies, dates and stamps; no local differences, aggregates or FX conversion. Pass native metric metadata and explicit source-backed units when available.

visual.name: dimensional-measures
visual.docs: Displays native per-coordinate valuation measures as bucket lists, two-axis matrices, and selectable three-axis slices. Uses Rust-supplied metric metadata for coordinates and units; exact values and canonical keys remain available.

visual.name: instrument-form
visual.docs: Standalone all-instrument generated form with grouped search, explicit examples and guarded recent selections. Lazy schema modules are reused by native module caching. Native validation is supplied by the consumer.

visual.name: pricing-params-form
visual.docs: Standalone controlled pricing parameters. Supply native groups from useModels and useMetrics(instrumentType). Selected metrics the type does not offer are reported, never dropped. Metric pricing overrides are edited from their schema and emitted as compact JSON. Market history text and omitted versus empty metric selection are preserved. JSON validation checks syntax only; native pricing owns financial validation.

visual.name: cashflow-viewer
visual.docs: Table of the supplied native cashflow envelope object with row-currency amounts and reporting-currency PV, validated against the Rust schema. Rust supplies totals and reconciliation. An optional ladder prop (the native cashflows.calendarYearLadder rows per row currency, as useCashflowLadder returns them) adds a Schedule / Annual ladder toggle with one table per currency in native PV. Envelope JSON (a host serialization of the object) is available for copy/download. Accepts cashflows, ladder, loading and error props; no worker or query provider required.

visual.name: explanation-trace
visual.docs: Optional original valuation explanation rendered losslessly; no steps or severity are inferred.

visual.name: valuation-details
visual.docs: Lazy native result detail routing. Only Monte Carlo has a complete published host shape; composite, credit, FX and structured-credit payloads stay raw. Unknown tags show a warning; full result metadata and nullable fields remain available.

visual.name: scenario-heatmap
visual.docs: Display returned ScenarioTable prices at original CPR/CDR coordinates, with an explicitly controlled severity and priceDomain straddling the canonical par reference 100. Prices are clean settlement percentages of current tranche balance per Rust ScenarioCell.price. Optional shared linking, callbacks, tooltip body, annotations and complete figure exports. No valuation, rebasing or WAL/writedown overlay.

visual.name: tranche-analytics
visual.docs: Present native valuations.instruments results for one tranche as supplied: the TrancheMetrics fields in Rust declaration order (unset optional fields hidden) with the unit each Rust field documents, any requested registry metrics raw, trancheBreakevenCdr and trancheDiscountMargin as decimals, and the trancheOas result. The clean price is a controlled exact-decimal input, percent of current balance; no price is assumed, and discount margin and OAS stay idle without one. OAS runs only through onSolveOas. With onOasConfigChange, an OAS configuration disclosure edits the generated OasConfig contract, starting from its Rust example (OasConfig::default()), and hands complete JSON to the host on apply. Nothing is computed, rescaled or defaulted. No worker is required.

visual.name: pricing-workbench
visual.docs: All-instrument workbench with complete market browser/editor, explicitly configured evaluated views, native calibration/diagnostics, linked residuals, validated market-to-pricing handoff and optional structured-credit tranche analytics (with an applied OasConfig) and scenarios over an editable ScenarioGrid seeded from the host grid. Host owns routes and domain inputs.

visual.name: pricing-forms-example
visual.docs: Standalone instrument and pricing forms with caller state and real shared worker hooks. Example installs at the consumer source directory under examples/ and receives the consumer-owned components alias. Fixture request derives from manifest-listed native instrument/market fixtures. No workbench block is imported.

visual.name: calibration-form
visual.docs: Editable canonical calibration envelope from the generated root, step and MarketQuote contracts. Requires explicit defaultJson and native validate callback; onSubmit receives canonical JSON only. Remount for a new document. No solver or business defaults are inferred.

visual.name: calibration-report
visual.docs: Present native report metrics, residual identities, diagnostics and structured failures without unit conversion. Accepts the published CalibrationReport; complete raw report metadata remains visible. Optional caller-owned linking uses [stepId, quoteId] keys.

visual.name: calibration-fit-chart
visual.docs: Plot signed returned residuals against zero in separate step and canonical quote-kind panels. Unmatched quote identities are isolated; missing quote-unit conventions are labeled solver units. Supports shared publication/export props, callbacks, tooltip slots and optional accepted selection.

visual.name: covenant-engine-editor
visual.docs: Composes schema-form over the generated covenant_engine contract (started from defaultJson; Rust publishes no example, so it otherwise starts empty). When loadTemplate is supplied, a template bar loads the specs of a Rust package (covenants.covLite, lboStandard, realEstate or projectFinance) for thresholds typed into decimal inputs that start empty; a blank threshold is sent as NaN and a rejected template shows the native error. Every metric_id and denominator_metric_id (top-level and windowed specs) is an id-combobox: free text with metricIds as suggestions. A Covenant metrics table lists each spec's metric id and whether metricIds contains it, before any evaluation; an unset metric id is listed as read by Rust's conventional metric for the covenant type and is not checked. Validation, templates and every term are native: connect validate to useCovenantEngineValidator, loadTemplate to useCovenantTemplate and onSubmit to the useEvaluateCovenants request. Accepts defaultJson, validate, onSubmit, loadTemplate, metricIds, disabled and density props.

visual.name: covenant-breach-forecast
visual.docs: Composes schema-form over the generated covenant_forecast_config contract (started from defaultConfigJson; Rust publishes no example and an empty config takes Rust's deterministic maintenance-scope defaults; Rust validates the config when it forecasts, so the form checks structure only and a uint64 random_seed stays exact) and a finstack-table of native FutureBreach rows (statements_analytics.forecastBreaches) in the order supplied, which Rust sorts by breach date, then covenant id: date, covenant, Rust's test description, projected value, threshold, headroom and breach probability with every supplied digit (a host may inject formatValue), an unset value as a dash. Deterministic forecasts list breached dates with probability 1; a stochastic config also lists dates whose probability reaches its breach_probability_threshold. Connect onSubmit to the useForecastBreaches request. Accepts defaultConfigJson, onSubmit, breaches, loading, error, formatValue and density props. No worker is required.

visual.name: covenant-compliance
visual.docs: Present native DatedCovenantReports rows (statements_analytics.evaluateCovenants over statement results, or CovenantEngine#evaluateSeries over dated rows) as a grid: one column per test date in the order supplied, one row per covenant instance key in first-appearance order, each cell the returned verdict as Passed or Failed, or a dash when Rust returned no report for that covenant on that date. A date header button selects the date (the latest initially) and its reports render below through covenant-report. Nothing is computed, sorted or inferred. No worker is required.

visual.name: covenant-report
visual.docs: Present native CovenantReport values keyed by covenant instance key (CovenantEngine#evaluate, one DatedCovenantReports row, or a valuation result's covenants) as a typed table in the order supplied: Rust's test description, actual value, threshold and headroom with every supplied digit (a host may inject formatValue), the passed verdict as Passed or Failed, and details; a field Rust leaves unset shows as a dash. The complete reports stay available as JSON in a Covenants disclosure. No verdict, headroom or threshold is computed. No worker is required.

visual.name: market-scenario-builder
visual.docs: Composes schema-form over the generated scenario_spec contract (started from defaultJson, else the Rust schema example), with IdCombobox on the operation curve_id, discount_curve_id, vol_surface_id, surface_id and ids fields: free text with the supplied market ids as suggestions, never filtered by kind. When templates is supplied, a picker lists scenarios.listBuiltinTemplateMetadata (useListBuiltinTemplateMetadata) with the selected template's returned description, severity, event date, asset classes and tags; Load template replaces the document with scenarios.buildFromTemplate or, for a chosen component, buildTemplateComponent, and Compose with scenario merges the current scenario and the template through scenarios.composeScenarios (Rust's priority order, id and hazard-bump-mode rule). Template ids are placeholders the user maps to market ids. When buildMarketScenario is supplied (useBuildMarketScenario), Add parallel shift and Add roll append the operations Rust builds (scenarios.parallelBpMany, operationSpecTimeRollForward); a blank size is NaN and a blank roll mode is omitted, so Rust rejects or defaults them. Validation is native (connect validate to useScenarioSpecValidator); onSpecChange receives the canonical spec, or null while an edit is pending or rejected, and the canonical spec is shown as JSON. Every failure is the native error. Accepts defaultJson, validate, onSpecChange, curveIds, templates, templatesError, buildFromTemplate, buildTemplateComponent, composeScenarios, buildMarketScenario, disabled and density props.

visual.name: market-scenario-report
visual.docs: Display-only view of the ApplicationReport returned by scenarios.applyScenario: operation and effect counters, every applied shock, the time roll with its returned per-instrument and total carry, every warning variant shown generically by kind and fields, the ResultsMeta stamp and the report JSON. Values are shown as returned; nothing is summed or converted. Accepts report, loading and error props; no worker or query provider required.

visual.name: horizon-return-report
visual.docs: Display-only view of the HorizonReport returned by scenarios.computeHorizonReturn (useHorizonReturn): total and annualized return and each factor contribution as the decimal fractions Rust computed (an undefined value, such as the annualized return without a time roll, reads "not defined", never zero), the horizon in calendar days, the exact initial and terminal values, the Rust explain text (scenarios.horizonResultExplainText), the attribution through pnl-attribution-report and the scenario application report through market-scenario-report in a disclosure. Nothing is computed here. Accepts report, explain, loading, error and density props; no worker or query provider required.

visual.name: pnl-attribution-report
visual.docs: Display-only view of a PnlAttribution as returned (by attribution.attributePnl / attributePnlMany, or inside scenarios.computeHorizonReturn): total, mark-to-market and endpoint values, every factor bucket as exact money with a signed bar chart of the returned amounts, the waterfall drawn only from Rust's waterfall_steps (pv_before to pv_after per step; nothing when the method returns none), the residual with the returned residual_pct and tolerances, notes, the policy stamp and the JSON. Optional explain, residualWithinTolerance and pctOfTotal props take Rust's pnlAttributionExplainText, pnlAttributionResidualWithinTolerance and pnlAttributionPctOfTotal; without residualWithinTolerance no verdict is shown. Nothing is summed, differenced or converted. Accepts attribution, loading, error and density props; no worker or query provider required.

visual.name: performance-report
visual.docs: Display-only view of the report returned by usePerformanceReport (analytics.Performance over a host-supplied panel). A ticker control selects the per-ticker sections. Lookback tiles show MTD, QTD, YTD and FYTD to the returned reference date; the summary is the returned TableEnvelope; cumulative returns (every ticker), drawdown, rolling series, monthly returns (heatmap) and annual returns are drawn against each ticker's own active dates; drawdown episodes are listed largest first. Values are the decimal fractions and ratios Rust returns, with no units inferred; non-finite values are left out of figures and shown as returned elsewhere. The monthly colour domain is the caller's, else the extent of the returned values. Accepts report, loading, error, initialTicker, monthlyDomain, formatValue and density props; no worker or query provider required.

visual.name: benchmark-report
visual.docs: Display-only view of the report returned by useBenchmarkReport (analytics.Performance against a named benchmark over a host-supplied panel). A fund control selects the ticker, defaulting to the first ticker that is not the benchmark. Key-value tables show the fund's greeks (alpha, beta, R squared, adjusted R squared, observations), its beta estimate with standard error and confidence bounds, and its tracking error, information ratio, Treynor, M squared, up and down capture, capture ratio and batting average. Cumulative outperformance and drawdown difference are drawn against the fund's own active dates, rolling alpha and beta against the returned window-end dates; the multi-factor regression (alpha, one beta per factor, R squared, adjusted R squared, residual volatility, observations) or its native error is shown when a factor panel was supplied. Values are the decimal fractions and ratios Rust returns, with no units inferred; non-finite values are left out of figures and shown as returned elsewhere. Accepts report, loading, error, initialTicker, formatValue and density props; no worker or query provider required.

visual.name: portfolio-summary
visual.docs: Display-only view of the valuation returned by useValuePortfolio (portfolio.valuePortfolio). Shows total_base_currency, the valuation date, fx_collapse_policy as the text Rust stamped, by_entity values in entity registration order (Portfolio#entityIds) and degraded_positions with each risk_error. Amounts are the exact returned money; nothing is summed or converted. Accepts report ({entityIds, valuation}), loading, error and density props; no worker or query provider required.

visual.name: positions-table
visual.docs: Display-only view of the valuation returned by useValuePortfolio. Rows follow Portfolio#positionIds (spec order), never the position_values key order: entity, instrument, native and base values, the FX rate Rust applied, risk completeness and inapplicable_metrics (metrics on the requested menu the instrument has no calculator for). Activating a row shows that position's returned valuation_result with valuation-summary and measures-grid; pass Rust metricMetadata (useMetricMetadata) for measure labels. Accepts report ({positionIds, valuation}), metadata, initialPosition, loading, error and density props; no worker or query provider required.

visual.name: portfolio-metrics
visual.docs: Display-only view of the metrics returned by useValuePortfolio (portfolio.aggregateMetrics) and a series from usePortfolioMetricsSeries (portfolio.portfolioMetricsSeries). The series is charted per first key component (the curve) with buckets in the order Rust returned them, which is lexical (10y, 15y, 1y, ...); no tenor sort is applied while tenor ordering is an open owner decision. Aggregated rows show each total with by-entity columns in entity registration order; the position table shows that position's raw metrics with its native currency. unaggregated_metrics, skipped_metrics and degraded_positions are listed as returned. Accepts report ({positionIds, entityIds, metrics}), series, metadata, initialPosition, formatValue, loading, error and density props; no worker or query provider required.

visual.name: scenario-pnl-table
visual.docs: Display-only view of the batch returned by useScenarioPnlBatch (portfolio.scenarioPnlBatch): rows in Portfolio#positionIds (spec) order, never the by_position key order, plus any position a scenario added in returned key order; one column per scenario in batch order with the exact returned by_position money; a total row from each scenario's returned pnl.total (base currency); a bar chart of those totals; and each scenario's ApplicationReport through market-scenario-report in a disclosure. Nothing is summed or differenced. Accepts report ({positionIds, items}), loading, error and density props; no worker or query provider required.

visual.name: portfolio-margin-report
visual.docs: Display-only view of the PortfolioMarginResult returned by usePortfolioMargin (portfolio.portfolioMargin): the total margin with an always-shown Indicative badge, every returned total (initial, variation, required and segregated IM collateral, IM transfer) as exact base-currency money, positions_without_margin and total_positions as the counts Rust returns, netting sets in returned order (id, methodology, position count, IM, VM, total and the returned is_approximate flag), IM collateral by CSA in the netting sets' CSA order (then any other returned CSA), degraded positions with Rust's messages, and for the selected netting set its im_breakdown and SIMM sensitivities through simm-sensitivity-table. Amounts are shown as returned, including a -0 variation margin; nothing is summed, netted or converted. Accepts result, loading, error and density props; no worker or query provider required.

visual.name: simm-sensitivity-table
visual.docs: Display-only view of a SimmSensitivitiesJson document (for example the canonical text useSimmSensitivitiesValidator returns, parsed). Sections follow the SIMM risk classes (interest rate, credit qualifying, credit non-qualifying, equity, commodity, FX); each holds the class's delta and vega tuples in input order, with columns named after the Rust tuple positions, and the curvature entries whose risk_class is that class. Empty fields are omitted. Nothing is summed, netted, regrouped or converted; amounts are in the set's base currency, which is shown. Accepts sensitivities, formatValue and density props; no worker or query provider required.

visual.name: simm-report
visual.docs: Display-only view of the ImResult returned by useSimmIm (margin.SimmCalculator#calculateFromSensitivities). The headline is the returned amount with methodology, as_of, mpor_days and the detail's mpor_scale. An Indicative badge is always shown, beside the returned approximation flag: the result is for indicative funding and capacity analysis, not for reconciling a counterparty margin call. The breakdown lists the returned component amounts as exact money in returned key order; the drill-down shows the returned risk_class_margins and, for a selected component, its buckets (k, signed_sum) and weighted sensitivities (risk weight, concentration factor). Nothing is aggregated. Accepts result, loading, error, formatValue and density props; no worker or query provider required.

visual.name: simm-calculator
visual.docs: Composes schema-form over the generated simm_sensitivities_json contract (started from defaultJson, else the Rust schema example), a date-input for the calculation date, simm-sensitivity-table over the natively validated canonical set and simm-report over the returned ImResult. Validation and calculation are caller callbacks: connect validate to useSimmSensitivitiesValidator and onSubmit plus result, loading and error to useSimmIm. Rust accepts only USD-based sets; another base currency surfaces the native error in the report. Accepts defaultJson, asOf, onAsOfChange, validate, onSubmit, result, loading, error, formatValue and density props.

visual.name: csa-editor
visual.docs: Composes schema-form over the generated csa_spec contract (started from defaultJson, else the Rust schema example). When loadPreset is supplied, a preset bar loads the Rust USD or EUR regulatory CSA (margin.csaSpecUsdRegulatory, csaSpecEurRegulatory) or regulatory terms for a typed currency, CSA id and collateral curve (margin.csaSpecRegulatory); the inputs start empty and a rejected preset shows the native error. Validation, presets and every term are native: connect validate to useCsaValidator, loadPreset to useCsaPreset and onSubmit to the useVm, useMarginCalls or useMarginCallDates request. Accepts defaultJson, validate, onSubmit, loadPreset and density props.

visual.name: margin-call-table
visual.docs: Display-only view of what useVm, useMarginCalls and useMarginCallDates return. The variation margin section shows the Rust call decision (margin.vmResultRequiresCall) as a badge, the Rust net margin (margin.vmResultNetMargin: post minus collect, positive when the desk posts) in the result's currency, the date and settlement date, and the VmResult money terms (gross exposure, threshold, independent amount, net exposure, collateral balance, unrounded call, MTA, rounding increment, post and collect amounts) as exact money. The margin calls section lists VmCalculator#generateMarginCalls in returned order; the call dates section lists VmCalculator#marginCallDates. Nothing is netted, thresholded or rounded. Accepts vm, calls, callDates, loading, error, formatValue and density props; no worker or query provider required.

visual.name: monte-carlo-diagnostics
visual.docs: Published MonteCarloValuationDetails only: native counts, flags, standard error, full-width bigint seed and time grid. Includes the native LSMC standard-error caveat.

visual.name: fx-surface-chart
visual.docs: Raw FX quotes and native evaluated Black volatility, sharing surface table/slices/selection/exports. Supply original coordinates with explicit quote/base forwards and an explicit color domain. Missing forwards show only raw quotes; no curve choice or local conversion occurs. The strike grid materializes the quotes natively (models.volatility.materializeFxDeltaSurface) from an editable spot (domestic per unit of foreign) and continuously compounded domestic and foreign decimal rates, seeded only from initialSpot, initialDomesticRate and initialForeignRate. Requires FinstackQueryProvider. Quote editing uses market-context-form and use-market-validator.

visual.name: vol-cube-slice
visual.docs: Slices a canonical cube at explicit absolute strikes (initialStrikes, one editable field each, in the given order) through models.volatility.materializeCube{Tenor,Expiry}Slice[Normal], rendered by the shared surface view with an explicit color extent per convention. The node smile comes from SabrSmile at the selected expiry/tenor node: normal volatility when beta < 1e-4, Black otherwise, as the facade documents; the arbitrage check needs an explicit continuously compounded decimal rate (initialRate, never defaulted) and the repaired line appears only when repairIterations is supplied. Strike ordering and domain are validated natively. Requires FinstackQueryProvider.

visual.name: surface-arbitrage-badge
visual.docs: Runs models.volatility.checkSurface (through useCheckSurface) on a canonical stored surface with host-supplied forwards (one to broadcast or one per expiry, in the surface strike units; never inferred) and an optional tolerance. The badge shows Passed, the violation count, Not checked (the native error, such as a normal-quoted, shifted-Black or tenor-axis surface Rust does not check) or Forwards not supplied (no request is made). The popover lists the returned counts by type and severity and every violation (type, severity, expiry, adjacent expiry, strike, magnitude in total variance, suggested fix, description) in the order Rust returned them. Requires FinstackQueryProvider.

visual.name: vol-cube-explorer
visual.docs: Checked native volatility cube exploration. Supply canonical cube state, initial absolute strike and explicit normal or Black/lognormal convention, plus color extents for both output units. Original SABR parameters, forwards and shifts remain separate from evaluated samples. Supplying slice (explicit initialStrikes, optional initialRate and repairIterations) adds vol-cube-slice. Requires FinstackQueryProvider; editing uses market-context-form and native validation.

visual.name: transition-matrix-heatmap
visual.docs: Display-only view of the results returned by useMigrationMatrix (models.credit.migration.TransitionMatrix.fromLabeled) and useMigrationProjection (GeneratorMatrix.fromTransitionMatrix, then models.credit.migration.project per horizon). Labels and the default state come from the matrix's RatingScale. The transition and generator matrices are heatmaps (origin by destination, scale order); probabilities use the colour domain [0, 1] and the generator the extent of its intensities, centred on zero when the negative diagonal and positive off-diagonals straddle it. The generator's round-trip error and L1 regularization are stamped beside it; cumulative default probabilities are drawn per origin state against the requested horizons. A view control switches every section to tables. A projection error (for example a round-trip tolerance Rust rejects) is shown inline while the matrix stays visible. Values are decimals as Rust returned them; nothing is computed. Accepts matrix, loading, error, projection, projectionLoading, projectionError, initialView, formatValue and density props; no worker or query provider required.

visual.name: merton-calculator
visual.docs: Edits a Merton structural-credit request: horizons, CDS maturity and recovery, and the model either with the schema form over the generated MertonModel contract (native validation through the caller's validate callback, usually useMertonModelValidator) or as a KMV equity calibration (equity value and volatility, short- and long-term debt, rate, payout, calibration maturity). Calculate passes the request to the caller (usually the useMertonReport request). The returned report is shown as Rust returned it: CDS par spread and implied equity value and volatility tiles, a term-structure table (default probability, distance to default, implied and debt spreads, master-scale grade and central PD per horizon) and the canonical model parameters with the KMV default point of an equity calibration. A measure Rust rejects for the model (such as the debt spread of a first-passage barrier) shows its native error beside the rest. Values are decimals with no units inferred. Accepts defaultRequest, validate, onSubmit, report, loading, error, formatValue and density props.

visual.name: credit-scorecard
visual.docs: Edits the input ratios of one accounting-based credit model (Altman Z-Score, Z'-Score, Z''-Score or EM-Score, Ohlson O-Score, Zmijewski probit). The fields, their order and their help text come from the generated input contract of the selected model (altman_z_score_input, altman_z_prime_input, altman_z_double_prime_input for both Z'' and EM, ohlson_o_score_input, zmijewski_input); each model keeps its own entries when another is selected. Score passes the model and the ratios to the caller (usually the useCreditScore request); typed text becomes numbers as entered and an empty field is sent as NaN for Rust to reject. The returned score, zone and implied PD are shown as Rust returned them, with the default PD master scale's grade and central PD of the implied PD, or Rust's error when the model returns no implied PD (the Altman models). Nothing is computed or classified here. Accepts defaultModel, defaultInputs, onSubmit, score, loading, error, formatValue and density props.

visual.name: portfolio-risk-report
visual.docs: Presents the report the worker positionRisk returns (usually through usePositionRisk): portfolio VaR, ES, confidence, method, position count and the Euler residual stamp (none for a historical decomposition); bars of each returned component VaR; the VaR contributions (component, relative, marginal and incremental VaR) and ES contributions tables; the risk budget (has_breach, total_overbudget and per-position actual and target component VaR, utilization and excess) when one was requested; and, for a historical source, the tail stress attribution (VaR threshold, tail scenario count, per-position tail contributions in Rust's largest-driver-first order and the tail scenarios worst first). A budget or stress attribution Rust rejects shows its native error beside the rest. Values are as returned: losses negative, in the units of the supplied weights or P&L, shares as fractions; nothing is summed, flagged or re-sorted. With factors (usually from useFactorRisk) it adds a Factor contributions section: total and residual risk under the returned measure, risk by factor (absolute, relative and marginal), risk by position and factor, any residual risk by position, and the portfolio.computeFactorSensitivities matrix it decomposed in the book's base currency; the factor chain's native error shows in that section. Either part renders without the other. Accepts report, factors, factorsError, loading, error, formatValue and density props.

visual.name: financial-model-editor
visual.docs: Edit explicit FinancialModelSpec fields from the generated Rust schema. Native WASM validates and canonicalizes the model; formula fields show the opaque native parse preview. Requires FinstackQueryProvider and remounting for a new document.

visual.name: statement-grid
visual.docs: Display schema-checked StatementResult values in a report-style table with historical and forecast columns, accounting presentation, and optional inline editing of explicit cells. Each cell shows the evaluation layer Rust recorded in node_sources (value, forecast, formula or where mask) as a glyph with a legend and accessible text; results without node_sources, such as rollups, show no marker. Exact native values, nonfinite sentinels, metadata, and the full result remain available. Editing is delegated to the host workbench for native validation and evaluation.

visual.name: statement-chart
visual.docs: Plot finite native values for one supplied statement node in explicit period order. Missing and nonfinite values are omitted from marks and remain visible in the grid; Money stays exact there. Selection links by node and period.

visual.name: statement-explanation
visual.docs: Call native explanation and dependency trace for a matching model/result/node/period request. Render the structured value, source, forecast, formula breakdown and dependency tree without parsing formulas in JavaScript.

visual.name: statement-check-report
visual.docs: Display native check summary, statuses, severity, findings and materiality without local pass/fail calculations. Supplied cell selection is a notification only; the full report remains exportable.

visual.name: statement-checks
visual.docs: Edit the check suite through the form generated from the Rust CheckSuiteSpec, validated natively before running; three-statement and credit mappings stay canonical JSON because Rust publishes no root for them. Native execution owns all check semantics and nothing is inferred from examples.

visual.name: variance-table
visual.docs: Present a native VarianceReport (for example ScenarioDiff.variance) as is: rows in native order, baseline and comparison columns under their native labels, abs_var as the variance and pct_var as a percent of the fraction Rust returns, with an unset pct_var (baseline effectively zero) shown as n/m. Metric labels default to labelFor; a host may inject metricLabel and formatValue. It sorts, totals and computes nothing. No worker is required.

visual.name: credit-assessment-report
visual.docs: Present a native CreditAssessment (statements_analytics.creditAssessment) as returned: tiles for leverage ratio, interest coverage and free cash flow at the assessed period, a line chart of the two ratios over the returned series (periods Rust returns without a value are left out of the chart and listed), and the series table with a dash for each missing value. A native P&L summary TableEnvelope (statements_analytics.plSummaryReport) renders below it through table-envelope when supplied. Free cash flow carries the host's model currency when one is passed; nothing is calculated, sorted or inferred. Accepts assessment, plSummary, currency, formatValue, loading, error, plSummaryLoading, plSummaryError and density props. No worker is required.

visual.name: tornado-chart
visual.docs: Present native TornadoEntry rows (for example DcfSensitivityResult.entries or generateTornadoEntries output) as returned: one band per parameter in Rust's order, a bar from zero to each returned downside and upside delta, and a table of the same values. Deltas Rust returns as non-finite are left out of the chart and shown in the table. Parameter labels default to labelFor; a host may inject parameterLabel and formatValue. It sorts, sums and computes nothing. Accepts entries, valueLabel, caption, parameterLabel, formatValue and density props. No worker is required.

visual.name: dcf-report
visual.docs: Present a native CorporateValuationResult (statements_analytics.evaluateDcf) as returned: enterprise value, equity value and per-share value tiles; the enterprise-to-equity bridge fields (net debt, valuation discount, diluted shares) and the equity bridge inputs Rust used, in Rust's order; the explicit forecast periods with their free cash flow, discount years, discount factor and present value, and the explicit present value; the undiscounted terminal value, its discount years and present value, and the WACC. A supplied DcfSensitivityResult (statements_analytics.dcfSensitivity) adds the baseline enterprise value, the effective WACC and terminal-growth shocks with their clamp flags, and a tornado-chart of the returned deltas. Monetary amounts keep Rust's exact decimal text; nothing is summed, discounted or rearranged. Accepts result, sensitivity, loading, error, sensitivityLoading, sensitivityError, sensitivityNote, formatValue and density props. No worker is required.

visual.name: dcf-assumptions-form
visual.docs: Edit the evaluateDcf assumptions: WACC as a decimal, the TerminalValueSpec variant (Gordon growth, exit multiple or H-model, the one hand-written Rust wire union) and its fields, the UFCF node and the exit-multiple metric node as id-comboboxes over the supplied model node ids, an optional net-debt override, and the remaining DcfOptions in the schema form over the generated contract. A cleared required number is sent as NaN, never 0; an empty optional value and empty options stay unset so Rust applies its defaults. The facade has no standalone DcfOptions parse, so the options are checked structurally here and validated by Rust (unknown keys included) when the model is valued. Calculate passes the submission to the caller (usually the useEvaluateDcf and useDcfSensitivity requests). Accepts defaultAssumptions, nodeIds, onSubmit, submitLabel, disabled and density props.

visual.name: lbo-report
visual.docs: Edit an LboConfig with the schema form over the generated lbo_config contract, every string *_node field as an id-combobox over the supplied model node ids. The facade has no standalone LboConfig parse, so the config is checked structurally here and validated by Rust (unknown keys included) when it is evaluated; Evaluate LBO passes the JSON to the caller (usually the useEvaluateLbo request). The native LboResult (statements_analytics.evaluateLbo) is shown as returned: equity check, exit equity proceeds and MOIC tiles, the sources and uses (debt, equity check, totals, entry enterprise value, the balanced flag), the entry and exit metrics, enterprise values and exit net debt, and the statement-check-report of the LBO checks when the config maps them. Returns are MOIC only: IRR is not part of the native result (Rust points to portfolio.mwrXirr). Nothing is calculated. Accepts defaultConfig, nodeIds, onSubmit, result, loading, error, formatValue and density props.

visual.name: statement-sensitivity
visual.docs: Edit a sensitivity run: the SensitivityMode (the wire values read from the generated sensitivity_result contract), the target metric as an id-combobox, the tornado period, and each varied node and period with comma-separated percentage moves. Each parameter's base value is read from the supplied evaluated result (a missing or non-finite cell is sent as NaN, never defaulted) and passed with the moves to statements_analytics.parameterSpecWithPercentages; an empty move is NaN, so Rust rejects it. Run sensitivity passes the run to the caller (usually the useRunSensitivity request). The native tornado is shown through tornado-chart, parameter keys (node@period) labelled by node and period, and the target metric at the tornado period in the baseline and every returned scenario in Rust's order. A full-grid run has no tornado; the scenarios are still shown. Nothing is calculated. Accepts result, nodeIds, periods, defaultValues, onSubmit, data, loading, error, disabled and density props.

visual.name: goal-seek-form
visual.docs: Edit statements_analytics.goalSeek arguments: target node and driver node as id-comboboxes over the supplied node ids, target and driver periods, the target value, and an optional lower and upper search bracket in the driver's units (both empty leave the bracket unset so Rust uses its own; a cleared number is sent as NaN, never 0). Solve passes the arguments to the caller (usually the useGoalSeek request); the native GoalSeekResult is shown as returned: solved value, residual, tolerance, evaluations and the converged flag. When onApply is supplied, Apply to model is a second, explicit action that hands the returned model (the input model with the solved driver written in) to the caller, such as the statements workbench's commit; there is no undo, and applyBlocked disables it with a reason. Nothing is calculated or defaulted. Accepts nodeIds, periods, defaultValues, onSubmit, result, loading, error, onApply, applyBlocked, disabled and density props.

visual.name: variance-bridge-chart
visual.docs: Present a native BridgeChart (statements_analytics.varianceBridge) as returned: a bar from zero to the baseline value, one signed bar from zero per driver contribution in Rust's order, a bar for Rust's unexplained residual and one for the comparison value, coloured by kind, with the same values in a table. Nothing is accumulated or positioned cumulatively: Rust's contributions are raw deltas in driver units, which need not sum to the target's variance, so this is not a waterfall. Non-finite values are left out of the chart and shown in the table. Node labels default to labelFor; a host may inject metricLabel and formatValue. Accepts bridge, metricLabel, formatValue and density props. No worker is required.

visual.name: forecast-backtest
visual.docs: Show a native ForecastMetrics (statements_analytics.backtestForecast) as returned: one tile per field in the generated forecast_metrics contract's order, labelled through labelFor with the first paragraph of Rust's description (MAPE and sMAPE are percentages in Rust). A null or non-finite metric, such as MAPE when every actual is zero, shows as n/m. Nothing is calculated. Accepts metrics, caption, loading, error and density props. No worker is required.

visual.name: statement-monte-carlo
visual.docs: Edit a MonteCarloConfig with the schema form over the generated monte_carlo_config contract (path count, the uint64 seed kept as an exact integer, percentiles and include path data; the form starts empty, Rust's example is not preloaded); Simulate passes the structurally valid JSON to the caller (usually the useEvaluateMonteCarlo request), and Rust validates it. The native MonteCarloResults (statements.Evaluator.evaluateMonteCarlo) are shown as returned: for the chosen metric (the first returned by default), a fan of bands between the returned percentiles paired from the outside in, with the unpaired middle percentile as a line, over the forecast periods, the percentile table (percentiles shown as percents of Rust's fractions), the breach probability Rust reports for a threshold (statements.monteCarloBreachProbability; null when the results carry no path data) and the simulation warnings in a collapsed list. Nothing is simulated, interpolated or summed. Accepts defaultConfig, onSubmit, results, loading, error, defaultBreach, onBreach, breachProbability, breachLoading, breachError, formatValue and density props.

visual.name: statements-workbench
visual.docs: Open on complete host-supplied financial statements with report-style inline editing, selectable periods, configurable native forecast methods, service-supplied roll forward with a native review since the last roll forward (variance, a variance bridge and a forecast backtest over the newly reported periods, offering only nodes present before and after), formula-backed calculated metrics with the active period's native credit assessment and P&L summary, a native DCF valuation with its enterprise-value tornado and a native LBO in Valuation, a native Monte Carlo of the stochastic forecasts with its percentile fan and breach probability in Monte Carlo, covenant compliance in Covenants (a covenant engine from defaultCovenantEngineJson or a Rust package template, tested by statements_analytics.evaluateCovenants at the end of every result period, with a metric the model lacks returned as Rust's not_found error, and a native breach forecast, statements_analytics.forecastBreaches, under a submitted CovenantForecastConfig), and checks. Scenarios override driver values and whole forecast specs and run natively, with the capital structure priced from the host market when one is supplied; each scenario shows its native lineage, and the active period's deltas against a chosen baseline (its parent by default) come from statements_analytics.scenarioDiff. Below the scenarios, a native sensitivity run ranks driver moves with a tornado, and a native goal seek solves for a driver value on Solve; applying the solved model is a separate, explicit action with no undo. The Annual view rolls results up natively: flows sum, balances take the year end and ratios are recalculated, with per-line methods editable. The schema editor and JSON import are in Advanced. density prop (compact default) sets SurfaceContext and data-density on the root; data-theme is inherited from the host. Host owns data ingestion and persistence. Requires FinstackQueryProvider.
